# Hypothermia on admission

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Indicator ID | `neo_hypothermia_admission` |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Status | Draft |
| Unit | Neonatal |
| Type | Process and outcome |
| Direction | Lower is better |
| Table | `qi.qi_neonatal_hypothermia_on_admission`, one row per site and admission month |

## Definition

The share of neonates whose temperature on admission was below 36.5 °C, among those with a plausible admission temperature recorded.

## Numerator

Neonates with an admission temperature below 36.5 °C. Column: `hypothermic`.

## Denominator

Neonates with a plausible admission temperature recorded (25 to 43 °C). Column: `assessed`.

## Exclusions

- Temperatures outside 25 to 43 °C, which are almost certainly typing errors (4.2 for 34.2). They are counted in implausible_temp and listed for the data managers to correct.
- Admissions without a usable admission date.

## Documentation completeness

The share of admissions with any admission temperature recorded (temp_recorded / admissions).

## Breakdowns

- WHO grade: mild 36.0 to 36.4 °C, moderate 32.0 to 35.9 °C, severe below 32.0 °C.

## REDCap fields

`temperature_degrees_celciu`, `date_adm`, `hosp_id`

## Why it matters

Hypothermia on admission is common, preventable and strongly linked to neonatal death. It reflects the warm chain from birth through transport to the newborn unit.

See [indicator conventions](README.md): suppression, empty rates, implausible values and completeness.
